settings.heading: A private commission
settings.text: The first cloth was chosen for how it held candlelight. From that fitting, a language of proportion followed: high collars, a measured shoulder, a hem that knows the floor without announcing it.

settings.heading: The atelier
settings.text: Work is done in small rooms. Patterns are walked around a person, not a dress form alone. We keep a ledger of cloth — origin, mill, and the evening it was first worn — so the house can remember what the calendar forgets.

settings.heading: A public wardrobe
settings.text: Friends asked to be dressed the same way. Maison Tavo opened so those requests could be answered with the same patience: limited editions, honest materials, and a storefront that behaves like a well-lit fitting room rather than a marketplace shout.

settings.heading: The invitation
settings.text: You are invited to read the journal, walk the lookbook, and take only what will be worn. The house is built in public now, but the standard remains private: would we keep this piece ourselves?

settings.heading: Our story
settings.lede: Maison Tavo began as a private wardrobe — pieces made for evenings that asked for composure, and mornings that asked for ease. The house opened when those pieces were requested by others.
